<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>I</c>ubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Exsultémus Dómino.

<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>L</c>et us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us glorify the Lord.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.

<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro Iob
<r>Iob 2:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Factum est autem, cum quadam die veníssent fílii Dei et starent coram Dómino, venísset quoque Satan inter eos et staret in conspéctu eius,
<n>2</n> Ut díceret Dóminus ad Satan: Unde venis? Qui respóndens ait: Circuívi terram et perambulávi eam.
<n>3</n> Et dixit Dóminus ad Satan: Numquid considerásti servum meum Iob, quod non sit ei símilis in terra, vir simplex et rectus ac timens Deum et recédens a malo et adhuc rétinens innocéntiam? Tu autem commovísti me advérsus eum, ut afflígerem eum frustra.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Si bona suscépimus de manu Dei, mala autem quare non sustineámus? Dóminus dedit, Dóminus ábstulit:
* Sicut Dómino plácuit, ita factum est: sit nomen Dómini benedíctum.
<r>℣.</r> Nudus egréssus sum de útero matris meæ et nudus revértar illuc.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut Dómino plácuit, ita factum est: sit nomen Dómini benedíctum.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Job
<r>Job 2:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> And it came to pass, when on a certain day the sons of God came, and stood before the Lord, and Satan came among them, and stood in his sight,
<n>2</n> That the Lord said to Satan: Whence comest thou? And he answered and said: I have gone round about the earth, and walked through it.
<n>3</n> And the Lord said to Satan: Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a man simple, and upright, and fearing God, and avoiding evil, and still keeping his innocence. But thou hast moved me against him, that I should afflict him without cause.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> What shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? The Lord gave and the Lord hath taken away. As the Lord hath pleased, so hath it befallen. Blessed be the Name of the Lord.
<r>℣.</r> Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither.
* The Lord gave and the Lord hath taken away. As the Lord hath pleased, so hath it befallen. Blessed be the Name of the Lord.

<r>Iob 2:4-6</r>

<r>℟.</r> Antequam cómedam, suspíro, et tamquam inundántes aquæ sic rugítus meus; quia timor, quem timébam, evénit mihi, et quod verébar áccidit. Nonne dissimulávi? nonne sílui? nonne quiévi?
* Et venit super me indignátio tua, Dómine.
<r>℣.</r> Ecce non est auxílium mihi in me, et necessárii quoque mei recessérunt a me.
<r>℟.</r> Et venit super me indignátio tua, Dómine.

b.879088fe04:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>S</c>éptimo Idus Septémbris Luna sexta. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>T</h>recis, in Gállia, sancti Nemórii Diáconi, et Sociórum Mártyrum, quos Attíla, Rex Hunnórum, interfécit.
<h>N</h>icomedíæ natális beáti Ioánnis Mártyris, qui, cum vidéret crudélia advérsus Christiános edícta in foro pendére, hinc, fídei ardóre accénsus, iniécta manu, illa detráxit atque discérpsit. Cumque hoc relátum esset Diocletiáno et Maximiáno Augústis, in eádem urbe constitútis, ómnia suppliciórum génera in eum experíri iussérunt; quæ vir nobilíssimus tanta vultus ac spíritus alacritáte pértulit, ut ne tristis quidem pro his vidéri potúerit.
<h>C</h>æsaréæ, in Cappadócia, sancti Eupsýchii Mártyris, qui, sub Hadriáno Imperatóre, accusátus quod Christiánus esset, in cárcerem coniéctus est; et, paulo post inde emíssus, patrimónium statim véndidit, et prétium partim paupéribus, partim accusatóribus, tamquam benefactóribus, distríbuit. Sed, íterum comprehénsus, atque, cum sacrificáre nollet idólis, sævíssime dilaniátus et gládio confóssus, sub Saprítio Iúdice martýrium consummávit.
<h>P</h>ompeiópoli, in Cilícia, sancti Sozóntis Mártyris, qui sub Maximiáno Imperatóre, in ignem iniéctus, réddidit spíritum.
<h>A</h>quiléiæ sancti Anastásii Mártyris.
<h>A</h>pud Aléxiam véterem, in território Augustodunénsi, sanctæ Regínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, sub Procónsule Olýbrio, cárceris et equúlei ac lampadárum afflícta supplíciis, demum, cápite damnáta, migrávit ad Sponsum.
<h>A</h>ureliánis, in Gállia, deposítio sancti Evórtii Epíscopi, qui, primo Románæ Ecclésiæ Subdiáconus, dehinc divíno múnere per colúmbam designátus est Póntifex præfátæ urbis.
<h>I</h>n Gállia sancti Augustális, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>C</h>ápuæ sancti Pámphili Epíscopi.
<h>I</h>n território Parisiénsi sancti Clodoáldi, Presbýteri et Confessóris.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.88d2a7cdee:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>S</c>eptember 7th 2027, the 6th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Troyes, the holy martyrs Nemorius the Deacon, and his Companions, who were slain by Attila, King of the Huns.
<h>A</h>t Nicomedia, the blessed martyr John. When he saw the cruel edicts against the Christians hanging up in the market-place, in the heat of his faith he stretched forth his hand, pulled them down, and tore them up. When this was told to the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, who were then in that city, they ordered all the kinds of torment to be tried upon him and the man, right noble as he was, bore this with such a cheerful face and heart that he seemed not even saddened thereby.
<h>A</h>t Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy martyr Eupsychius, who was cast into prison under the Emperor Hadrian on the charge of being a Christian. Being shortly liberated therefrom, he forthwith sold his inheritance, and distributed the price thereof partly unto the poor, and partly unto his accusers, as unto benefactors. He was arrested again, and finished his testimony under the judge Sapritius, being mangled, and pierced with the sword.
<h>A</h>t Soli, in Cilicia, the holy martyr Sozon, who under the Emperor Maximian was cast into the fire, and gave up the ghost.
<h>A</h>t Aquileia, (in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian,) the holy martyr Anastasius.
<h>I</h>n the country of Autun, the holy Virgin and martyr Regina, who passed away to Christ the Bridegroom under the Proconsul Olybrius, by whose orders she was imprisoned, racked, burnt with lamps, and lastly beheaded.
<h>A</h>t Orleans, in Gaul, holy Bishop Evortius, who was first a Subdeacon of the Church of Rome, and was then pointed out by the vision of a dove for Bishop of the aforesaid city.
<h>I</h>n Gaul, the holy Confessor Bishop Augustal.
<h>A</h>t Capua, holy Pamphilus, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>I</h>n the country of Paris, (in the sixth century,) the holy Priest and Confessor Clodoald (St. Cloud) .
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Ant.</r> My soul * magnifies the Lord, because God has regarded my lowliness.
<r>Canticle of the Blessed Virgin</r>
<r>Luke 1:46-55</r>
§00.83742356bc
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> My soul magnifies the Lord, because God has regarded my lowliness.
b.78720bca14:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>T</c>ua nos, quǽsumus, Dómine, grátia semper et prævéniat et sequátur: ac bonis opéribus iúgiter præstet esse inténtos.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.92ee18cc40:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>L</c>ord, we pray thee, that thy grace may always prevent and follow us, and make us continually to be given to all good works.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoratio B. Bertrandi a Garriga, Confessoris O. P.</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Euge, serve bone et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam, dicit Dóminus.

<r>℣.</r> Iustus germinábit sicut lílium.
<r>℟.</r> Et florébit in ætérnum ante Dóminum.

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui sancto Patriarchæ Domínico beátum Bertrándum, Confessórem tuum, sócium et imitatórem exímium adiúnxísti: eius nobis pio intervéntu concéde ita eiúsdem sequi vestígia, ut assequámur et prǽmia.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.

<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.

<c>L</c>et us pray.

<r>Commemoration of B. Bertrandi a Garriga, Confessoris O. P.</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Well done, thou good and faithful servant thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things, saith the Lord.

<r>℣.</r> The just shall spring as the lily.
<r>℟.</r> And shall flourish for ever before the Lord.

<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, who didst join blessed Bertrand thy Confessor to the holy Patriarch Dominic as his companion and outstanding imitator: grant us by his loving intercession so to follow the footsteps of the same Patriarch that we may also attain his rewards.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
